summary: This article explains where the marathon got its name and how runners train, fuel their bodies, drink enough water, and pace themselves to finish a 42-kilometer race.
introduce: Start a K-W-L chart on the board and ask students what they already Know and what they Want to know about the topic of “Running a Marathon”. Tell them they will fill in what they Learned after reading.

keyTerms.def: how far it is from one place to another
an old story that may be only partly true
the ability to keep going for a long time

challengeTerms.def: a person who carries news or information to someone else
slowly, a little at a time
a form of sugar the body stores in the muscles and liver to use as fuel

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that anyone can run a marathon if they train well? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Imagine a friend is going to run a marathon. Write advice about endurance, water, and pace.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review distance, legend, and endurance, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses messenger, gradually, and glycogen to connect the article to something they learned in another subject.
